Manufactured.title: Manufactured
Manufactured.teaser: Textile influences, everyday objects, and the collector’s part in the work.

sections.title: From textile to code
paragraphs: Manufactured began with an attraction to textile patterns and textures. In a May 2024 reflection, Lemonhaze traced that attraction to Gunta Stölzl and the Bauhaus movement.

The possibility of an artwork becoming part of everyday life—a rug, a beach towel, a phone background—fed a wider critique of prefabricated art-market products. The collection’s texture and its questions about art as a commodity developed together.
The textile reference also prompted a physical experiment: in April 2024, Lemonhaze ordered a fabric sample to see the work beyond the screen.

sections.title: A release with consequences
paragraphs: The April 2024 release used the Bitcoin halving as a deadline. In the artist’s account after the halving, the 103 unsold works were to be sent to Satoshi’s address. The images remained publicly visible even as those works left circulation.

Games extended that relationship: collectors give up three Manufactured works to bring one personally dedicated Game into existence. The release figures in the original posts are historical; the Supply & Marketplace page records the site’s current circulation figures.

Games.title: Games
Games.teaser: A collector ritual, a changing supply, and a diary written one Game at a time.

sections.title: Three works become one
paragraphs: Games explores scarcity, collector experience and artistic integrity through a concrete exchange: three Manufactured works are burned to commission one custom Game. The Game is personally signed and dedicated, using extended Manufactured features, heavier brushes and textures, and a different frame ratio.

The May 2025 account describes two stages. In 2024, collectors chose from personal selections presented in galleries made for them. In 2025, the artist curated 90 + 9 final outputs, presented in La Boutique, inscription #94,082,594, with private tours and audio conversations.

That account sets a maximum of up to 101 Games, made on demand, with an annual April 20–September 8 season. It documents the project’s stated framework at that time; individual inscription dates are preserved with the works.

sections.title: Game Nº26 · Edo
paragraphs: Before choosing this output, artist and collector walked through the OnCyber gallery together on an audio call. The inscription note returns to their shared appreciation of Japan and Thailand, and the prospect of meeting again in Asia.

sections.title: Game Nº27 · A number becomes personal
paragraphs: While writing Game Nº27, Lemonhaze connected its number to the birth of his son on August 27. The dedication links the continuation of the collector ritual with fatherhood and the uncertainty of what comes next.

sections.title: Game Nº12 · A dedication to a friend
paragraphs: The first Game of 2025, output GR2-99, was inscribed for Maciej. Its dedication thanks him for the friendship, shared memories and immeasurable positive effect he had on the artist’s life and journey. The collector ritual becomes a personal gesture of gratitude.

sections.title: Game Nº28 · A strange game
paragraphs: The original inscription pairs a short reflection on escaping an imposed game with a quiet diary entry: “My Love picked this one, how peaceful.” It is dated September 11, 2026, in Griffintown, Montreal.
quotes: Getting out of the water is the only winning move.

Tad Small.title: Tad Small
Tad Small.teaser: How small files changed the way the artist worked with Bitcoin.

sections.title: Creating for Bitcoin
paragraphs: In May 2023, larger works had become too expensive to inscribe. Tad Small was a practical response: three small pixel works that let Lemonhaze continue creating while working within the cost and file-size constraints of Bitcoin.

Looking back in December 2024 and in Gentleman SE 2025, he describes this as a change in perspective: creating for the medium and adapting his tools, rather than only trying to fit an existing image onto the chain. The micro-canvases led into other small, digitally hand-drawn series during summer 2023.

sections.title: Casa Flamingo · A place in pixels
paragraphs: Casa Flamingo is an experimental pixel abstraction of the artist’s casita in Puerto Escondido. In his April 2026 post, he describes it as one of the defining works of his early journey.

Berlin.title: Berlin
Berlin.teaser: A night in 2018, a cultural meeting place, and the beginnings of My Love.

sections.title: 99 Francs · The first night
paragraphs: 99 Francs remembers the artist’s arrival in Berlin in 2018. A bottle of wine brought from the airport became a conversation with a French woman at his Airbnb, followed by a visit to a Russian bar-lounge. The French book and film they discussed gave the work its title.

sections.title: Revaler Straße 99 · RAW
paragraphs: The title points to the RAW cultural hub in Friedrichshain. Lemonhaze recalls its old industrial buildings, graffiti, music and free spirits as part of an unforgettable stay.

sections.title: The journey of a palette
paragraphs: My Love began with Gentleman Nº1 in March 2023. For 99 Francs in June, Lemonhaze sampled those colors, lightened the sand, deepened the red, blue and turquoise, and removed the faux-fuchsia.
After using this palette in Old-Fashioned, Oaxaca and Unregulated Minds, he introduced Deep Pink (#E91E63) for Five Roses in January 2024. The palette ties these works together across collections.

sections.title: From Berlin to Saigon · A composition evolves
paragraphs: In the HTML of From Berlin to Saigon, Lemonhaze describes the hand-drawn Berlin works as an enduring influence on his sense of composition. He followed an interest in dark ink-like structures and reflective shapes through drawing, AI and eventually p5.js.

A June 2024 visit to HOKMA in Hong Kong brought another connection: characters he could not read became abstract marks to his eye. Paper, ink and brush pens fed the visual feeling he later pursued in an output generated in Saigon.

sources.label: Original inscription · From Berlin to Saigon

Lotus.title: Lotus
Lotus.teaser: The other half, the aspiration of Gentlemen, and a return in Flashback.

sections.title: The reason to become a gentleman
paragraphs: The original Lotus statement is a dedication to the artist’s other half. Its image of a flower emerging from murky water connects beauty, strength and resilience with the aspiration expressed in Gentlemen.

That connection reappears inside Flashback: Part 3 reproduces the Lotus statement and lists the inscription IDs of all nine Lotus works. The earlier collection remains present within a later, more extensive piece of writing.
quotes:
Emerging from the depths of murky waters with pristine petals, Lotus is inspired by my other half, who remains pure in spite of it all.
The Lotus embodies beauty, strength, and resilience - a symbol of the women's experience. My reason to become a gentleman.

Old-Fashioned.title: Old-Fashioned
Old-Fashioned.teaser: Large images, compact inscriptions, and the emergence of the written header.

sections.title: Scale through recursion
paragraphs: Old-Fashioned combines very small HTML inscriptions with the ability to generate very large images. In September 2024, Lemonhaze described exports around 20,000 × 20,000 pixels, with generated PNG sizes of roughly 300–650 MB, from HTML inscriptions under 1 KB using recursion.

Those figures describe the generated image, rather than a hundreds-of-megabytes PNG stored as one inscription. The artist later noted that a work could take up to 90 seconds to load. Its scale asks the viewer to give it time.

sections.title: 1961 · Learning to leave a note
paragraphs: The header of 1961 contains “Like Father, Like Son.” In a January 2025 reflection on the work, Lemonhaze recalled that early notes were not always signed or developed beyond a title.
He places the shift toward HTML and p5.js in September 2023, crediting the OnChainMonkey and huuep library. Writing in the header gradually became a larger part of the work itself.

In June 2026, he returned to 1961 and its “Like Father, Like Son” header after seeing his father for the first time in over twelve years. This later reflection gives the 2023 work another point of connection with his life.

sections.title: An early exhibition
paragraphs: Lemonhaze identifies the August 2023 Ordinals Summit in Singapore as the first IRL exhibition of his works, with Old-Fashioned in the account.

Oaxaca.title: Oaxaca
Oaxaca.teaser: Puerto Escondido, surf and sun, and a Sunday returned to over time.

sections.title: A home in small textures
paragraphs: The original collection statement describes Puerto Escondido through a simple life of surf and sun. Geometric micro-textures are the means of paying homage to the place Lemonhaze called home for several years.

The writing is specific about the setting: nature, culture and simplicity in Oaxaca. The titles lead into that setting, while the recurring Sunday post gives one work a place in the artist’s weekly rhythm.

sections.title: A palette carried between places
paragraphs: Oaxaca is one of the series in which Lemonhaze used the My Love palette developed in 99 Francs, before adding Deep Pink in Five Roses. The palette carries a thread between Berlin, Oaxaca and Montreal.

Tori no Roji.title: Tori no Roji
Tori no Roji.teaser: The transition between Osaka’s busy streets and its quiet alleys.

sections.title: The Alleys of the Streets
paragraphs: Tōri no Roji — 通りの路地 — is the artist’s attempt to capture the contrast and transition between Osaka’s bustling streets and its quiet, hidden, charming alleys. The focus is the passage between those two experiences of the city.

Ma ville en quatre temps.title: Ma ville en quatre temps
Ma ville en quatre temps.teaser: Four seasons, rough images, and textures built with code.

sections.title: Images inside the code
paragraphs: For Ma ville en quatre temps, Lemonhaze describes converting images to Base64 and integrating them with code-based elements. Compression, roughness, distortion and pixelation can be intentional: those imperfections are blended with textures to make the finished high-resolution image.
HTML also preserves the writing. In his December 2025 explanation, the notes embedded in the header are a core reason to keep using this format. The visual and the text belong together.

The series was part of Continuum, The Forever Calendar, presented by Gamma at Inscribing Vegas 2025. Its four seasonal titles move through winter nights, summer in Montreal, a return to class, and autumn.

Little Get Away.title: Little Get Away
Little Get Away.teaser: An escape from obsession, accompanied by small personal notes.

sections.title: Stepping back
paragraphs: The original statement describes a need to step back from the things that obsess the artist, and a planned getaway with his love. The individual headers preserve short, sometimes uneasy thoughts alongside that wish.
Hollywood Moon is the parent inscription. Its note remembers “Hollywood” as the artist’s high-school nickname; the other works hold brief fragments rather than a continuous explanation.

Volatility.title: Volatility
Volatility.teaser: Emotional peaks and troughs, family memories, and messages to a future reader.

sections.title: The search for balance
paragraphs: Volatility’s original statement draws a parallel between market fluctuations and emotional life: euphoria, despair, hopes and dreams. Its subject is the search for balance within those changes.
The individual notes make that statement personal. They move between beach-life captions, memories of family, travel, and a greeting to someone reading the inscription far in the future.

sections.title: An inscription addressed to the future
quotes: I always wondered "how" were the people back in the days, for example 200-500-1000 years ago. Now I think it's always more or less the same. Everything, or at least almost everything in life is mathematic. Reality minus expectaction = happiness, at any point in time. If you read this from the future, hello my dear friend, may this world bring you the joy that I have the chance to appreciate today. FNST

Candidly Yours.title: Candidly Yours
Candidly Yours.teaser: Hand-drawn sketches meet p5.js textures and candid written reflections.

sections.title: Old and new tools together
paragraphs: Primitive documents small, digitally hand-drawn compositions upscaled and textured with p5.js. Its header identifies the original 288 × 512 sketch inside the code as Base64, alongside a high-resolution export.

In Coral, Lemonhaze describes the pleasure of drawing by hand again after concentrating on code, and of bringing old and new tools together. Printemps closes the series by describing each work as a snapshot of introspection, inspiration and personal reflection.

sections.title: La Carte · Work and its rewards
paragraphs: La Carte refers to the time cards once used by workers. Its abstraction draws on a vague visual memory of those cards.

The inscription’s note begins with something Lemonhaze’s father used to tell him: work hard, then reap the fruits of your labour. The artist follows it with a question—does that promise really hold for workers? A familiar object becomes a way to revisit an inherited belief.
quotes: Travailler fort pour ensuite recolter les fruits de son labeur. Mais est-ce vraiment le cas pour les ouvriers? FNST

Downtown.title: Downtown
Downtown.teaser: A craving for the city, preserved in two short inscription notes.

sections.title: Getting a city fix
paragraphs: The note in Downtown (Zero) catches a particular impulse: craving the city and considering a few days in Mexico City. Good Night records the more ordinary moment of having worked for days and forgotten to inscribe the piece.
Read together, these small notes place the works within the artist’s daily rhythm—wanting a change of scene, working, and finally putting the image on-chain.

Orphelinat.title: Orphelinat
Orphelinat.teaser: Hosoi, Paris, and the personal writing behind these early individual works.

sections.title: Hosoi · A thin line
paragraphs: Hosoi’s original note describes the thin line between what keeps the artist alive and what harms him. It speaks of addiction, losing sight of things, pushing people away, and uncertainty over whether staying is selfish or an unwillingness to give up.
Hosoi sold for 0.5 BTC, Lemonhaze’s highest primary sale to date.

In a December 2025 reflection on his process, Lemonhaze identifies Hosoi and Eclosion as his first works using this technique of converting images to Base64, before his first parent-child collection, Untitled, in 2023.

sections.title: Paris · Here and elsewhere
paragraphs: The inscription opens with a quotation from Friendly Fires’ song Paris, followed by the artist’s own French note. Being present and absent at once becomes an apology to the person he loves. It is a short, direct expression of ambition, uncertainty and the hope of being understood.
Paris was included in OCM’s Digital Rosetta Stone.

quotes.text: One day we're gonna live in Paris
quotes.credit: Friendly Fires, “Paris” · quoted in the inscription

quotes: Je m'excuse d'etre la, mais pas la en meme temps. Je ne sais pas quoi faire d'autre, I want it so bad. J'espere que tu comprends, je t'aime. FNST

sections.title: Deprivation · Original and prints
paragraphs: The original Deprivation sits within Orphelinat. A separate Deprivation (Prints) collection carries the image into an edition. The print collection’s statement describes a soul caught between passion and obsession, longing for light through sleepless nights.

Deprivation (Prints).title: Deprivation (Prints)
Deprivation (Prints).teaser: The original work, the edition, and a statement about sleepless nights.

sections.title: Between passion and obsession
paragraphs: The print collection’s original statement places deprivation between passion and obsession: a longing for light amid sleepless nights. That statement gives an entry into the work without turning its edition history into a different origin story.
The original Deprivation belongs to Orphelinat. The works in this gallery are the separate print edition; their inscription records distinguish the individual prints from the original.

Polaroid.title: Polaroid
Polaroid.teaser: An image made after New York’s wildfire-smoke sky.

sections.title: Polaroid #8 · June 2023
paragraphs: Lemonhaze recalls making Polaroid #8 on June 8, 2023, after New York’s sky filled with wildfire smoke. When he returned to the work in July 2026, a similar sky brought that moment back.

DeVille.title: DeVille
DeVille.teaser: Cypherville creatures revisited through images, code and their original descriptions.

sections.title: Each descendant remembers its ancestor
paragraphs: Deville combines AI, Krita and p5.js. Each work recursively references its ancestor creature from Cypherville, while the HTML header preserves that creature’s original February–March 2023 description.
The relationship is both visual and written: the earlier creature is referenced inside the later inscription, and its description travels with it.

sections.title: A gift to the creature’s keeper
paragraphs: For Cypherville’s second anniversary in February 2025, Lemonhaze announced the final batch of DeVille works, together with unclaimed works from 2024. Each was to go to the address holding its corresponding creature—a gesture to the collectors who had accompanied the project.

Cypherville.title: Cypherville
Cypherville.teaser: A creature kept in reserve, and descendants given to the original collectors.

sections.title: Creature #21 · More than three years later
paragraphs: Creature #21 was the one Lemonhaze had intended to keep. When he closed the original collection at sixteen pieces, it remained uninscribed. In June 2026, it finally reached Bitcoin as the cover of the collection’s inscribed gallery, more than three years later.
The cover belongs to the later gallery inscription; it does not turn the original sixteen-creature release into a twenty-one-piece collection.

sections.title: Descendants that remember
paragraphs: DeVille reconnects each later work with its Cypherville ancestor through recursion and the original creature description. The anniversary distribution brought those descendants back to the holders of the corresponding creatures.

Untitled.title: Untitled
Untitled.teaser: The first parent-child collection, with notes about love, memory and distance.

sections.title: Images gain a family
paragraphs: Lemonhaze identifies Untitled as his first collection with grand-parent-child provenance. In a later account of his process, he places it after Hosoi and Eclosion, his first experiments with this technique of converting images to Base64.

sections.title: Ten years, and the life beyond the sunset
paragraphs: Avant le Crepuscule was written on the eve of the tenth anniversary of the artist’s relationship. The sunset becomes an uncertain threshold: another life may be waiting beyond it, but he cannot yet tell what that life will be.

La Pomme Pourrite returns to the same relationship through gratitude. His partner saw more than a “rotten apple” in him; ten years later, she remains his reason to become a gentleman. Other notes move between the pleasure of shared places, solitude, and memories he would rather leave behind.

Le Bar a Tapas.title: Le Bar a Tapas
Le Bar a Tapas.teaser: Handcrafted mementos of Tenerife, made within Bitcoin’s fee constraints.

sections.title: From minimalist to ordinalist
paragraphs: The original statement places Le Bar à Tapas in Tenerife. High inscription fees prompted Lemonhaze to find new ways of creating for Bitcoin, using handcrafted works to preserve simple moments of his time in Spain.
Tenerife itself was inscribed on May 31, 2023, as inscription #10,267,494. The place, the small scale and the practical constraints are all part of this early period of adaptation.

Mending Fragments.title: Mending Fragments
Mending Fragments.teaser: Fragmented portraits and an early experiment in drawing for Bitcoin.

sections.title: Healing through fragments
paragraphs: The collection’s statement describes fragmented pieces coming together through healing and resilience, finding beauty within imperfection.

In Gentleman SE 2025, Lemonhaze places Mending Fragments alongside Berlin and Polaroid in the summer of 2023: digitally hand-drawn experiments that followed Tad Small. Small files made it possible to keep inscribing, while the process helped him learn new tools and connect with collectors.

The Artifacts.title: The Artifacts
The Artifacts.teaser: Early mixed-media works and the visual ideas that continued into later code.

sections.title: Ideas carried forward
paragraphs: Looking back in Gentleman SE 2025, Lemonhaze describes some Artifacts as mixed-media works made with AI and Krita. Their large files were part of the reason he explored p5.js: he wanted the highest-quality artwork to remain available on-chain.

The header of From Berlin to Saigon identifies Blood, Lemon & Tango, Le Dessinateur and Playa Zicatela among the earlier works that led toward its ink-like structures and textured compositions. These works form part of an explicitly documented visual progression.

sources.label: Original inscription · From Berlin to Saigon

Eclosion 1/1 - Amsterdam Blooms.title: Eclosion 1/1 - Amsterdam Blooms
Eclosion 1/1 - Amsterdam Blooms.teaser: An early Base64 experiment, made for Amsterdam Blooms.

sections.title: The flourishing future
paragraphs: Eclosion is a 2023 contribution to Amsterdam Blooms with Inscribing Atlantis. Its original statement describes “the flourishing future we imagine for ourselves.”

Lemonhaze later identified Eclosion and Hosoi as his first works using this technique of converting images to Base64, followed by Untitled. The work is an early link between the image and code parts of his practice.

1 of 1s (2024).title: 1 of 1s (2024)
1 of 1s (2024).teaser: Travel photographs, Montreal memories, and the progression from drawing to code.

sections.title: Photographs become a starting point
paragraphs: Saint-Laurent begins with a photograph taken by the artist’s partner during a bike ride from Brossard toward Montreal, around 2014 or 2015. It had already served as the cover of his song of the same name. In 2024, he returned to it as a starting point for combining travel photographs with his p5.js structures.
Somewhere in Hong Kong also uses a photograph taken by his partner. Its note records a wish to make more art about what surrounds him.

sources.label: Original inscription · Somewhere in Hong Kong

sections.title: Soir d’hiver · Remembering Montreal
paragraphs: The original French note ties winter romance to cold air, moonlight, rosy cheeks and songs by Dumas. Written after almost three years away, it returns in memory to Montreal’s old port and the air beside the river.

sections.title: From Berlin to Saigon · Following an idea
paragraphs: In the HTML of From Berlin to Saigon, Lemonhaze describes the hand-drawn Berlin works as an enduring influence on his sense of composition. He followed an interest in dark ink-like structures and reflective shapes through drawing, AI and eventually p5.js.

A June 2024 visit to HOKMA in Hong Kong brought another connection: characters he could not read became abstract marks to his eye. Paper, ink and brush pens fed the visual feeling he later pursued in an output generated in Saigon.

sources.label: Original inscription · From Berlin to Saigon

sections.title: Insaisissable Mirage · Always another horizon
paragraphs: The work’s writing asks what keeps the artist moving when reaching one goal only leads to another. Its November 2024 diary places that question on the balcony of an apartment in Vung Tau, alongside the quieter daily rhythm of cooking and spending time with his partner.

sections.title: Wondrous Place · An inscription from the balcony
paragraphs: On the work’s second anniversary, Lemonhaze recalled inscribing Wondrous Place from the balcony of his apartment in “Sin City” on July 25, 2024. The HTML quotes Billy Fury’s Wondrous Place (Catching Flies Remix).

1 of 1s (2025).title: 1 of 1s (2025)
1 of 1s (2025).teaser: A leap in technique, and writing that continues alongside the images.

sections.title: Progress gives the earlier work its context
paragraphs: In December 2025, Lemonhaze described Ma ville en quatre temps, Minute, papillon! and Chanchanok’s Temple as a leap in his use of techniques and tools. His belief that the best work is always the next one does not diminish the earlier work: it is the progression that gives the journey meaning.

Minute, papillon! and Chanchanok’s Temple were made during the same period with the same technique. The artist later described their personal significance, and identified Minute, papillon! as his submission to the 2025 Lumen Prize.

sections.title: Three works · Fracture, choice and movement
paragraphs: Glass Breaker, Mending Out and Off-Kilter each pair an abstract with a dated diary entry from April 22, 2025, in Jomtien Beach, Thailand. Their texts move through fracture, the choice to keep going, and movement within imbalance.
Off-Kilter also records the practical work behind the release: Lemonhaze thanks Pawel Dudko and Nathan Cornes (wageDu) for helping fix the earlier version’s mobile display issue.

Trilogy (Prints).title: Trilogy (Prints)
Trilogy (Prints).teaser: Three works, with distinct texts, brought together in a set of prints.

sections.title: Glass Breaker · Mending Out · Off-Kilter
paragraphs: Trilogy brings together three works in a set of 33 prints. Glass Breaker describes a moment of fracture; Mending Out turns toward choice after denial; Off-Kilter finds movement in imbalance.

The original works’ headers also preserve diary entries dated April 22, 2025, in Jomtien Beach. In Off-Kilter, the artist thanks Pawel Dudko and Nathan Cornes (wageDu) for helping fix a mobile display issue with the previous version. The prints and original works have separate inscription records.

Mirage (Prints).title: Mirage (Prints)
Mirage (Prints).teaser: Happiness, hope and the distance between dreams and reality.

sections.title: The promise of a mirage
paragraphs: The original statement describes an interplay between true happiness and misleading hope, locating fulfillment in the balance between dreams and reality. That tension is the stated subject of this print edition.

The edition is linked to its original work through the site’s provenance records. The later inscription of a collection gallery is part of the archive’s history, rather than the creation date of each print.

Discography.title: Discography
Discography.teaser: An unfinished soundtrack, with a recorded history of works leaving circulation.

sections.title: The soundtrack of a life
paragraphs: Lemonhaze’s original description calls Discography “The soundtrack of my life (unfinished).” The titles preserve those musical references within the collection.

In his July 23, 2025 burn announcement, the artist named Dreams, Anything in Return, Alchemy, The Chronic, Sexuality and I Created Disco. Their continued presence in this archive preserves the work and its history; it does not imply that those inscriptions remain in circulation.

World Tour.title: World Tour
World Tour.teaser: An unfinished homage to the countries the artist has travelled.

sections.title: Places remembered
paragraphs: The original statement describes World Tour as “An homage to the countries I’ve traveled (unfinished).” It gives the place names a direct autobiographical frame.

The July 23, 2025 burn announcement includes Oz, Germany, American Dream and Je me souviens under World Tour. The collection remains viewable here as an archive of the works, including those that left circulation.

1 of 1s (2026).title: 1 of 1s (2026)
1 of 1s (2026).teaser: An encrypted self-portrait and the idea of a work addressed to the future.

sections.title: Self-Portrait · A time capsule
paragraphs: In his February 2026 explanation of Self-Portrait, inscription #121,070,041, Lemonhaze describes the visible interface as a shell around encrypted content. He frames it as a time capsule—a gift for whoever may one day open it. Until then, the viewer encounters the void.

The artist’s technical account specifies AES-256-GCM with a key derived through Argon2id and a passphrase required to open the content. The concealed image and the act of waiting are part of the work’s premise.
